description:
Harden the transactional repository-materialization subsystem delivered by the repository-materialization epic to a verifiably correct and maintainable shape, acting on the adversarial audit recorded in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md`.

## Background

An adversarial audit of the completed repository-materialization epic (implementation grade B+, maintainability C+) found that the subsystem's strongest guarantees are narrated rather than enforced. The claimed single planning boundary is seven public plan-producing entry points across five error types; the capture/plan/apply/retry protocol is a hand-copied convention at 29 call sites with 65 bespoke conflict arms; typed errors round-trip through string form and runtime downcasts; the transaction kernel bridges two hand-aligned action enums with `unreachable!` panics on the publication path; the plan-derivation core has no property-based coverage; and every published performance figure is a single self-attested measurement. The audit also found nine falsifiable errors in the epic's showcase presentation and an epic-completion "independent" review that was performed by the building agent itself.

This epic collapses the planning boundary to match its claim, converts narrated guarantees into enforced tests, establishes performance as a maintained artifact-backed contract, clears the recorded hygiene debt, and replaces the showcase presentation with a corrected successor whose every claim traces to a repository artifact. The audit document is the finding-level source of truth; its Part C grouping (C1–C5) is the scope inventory.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A single mutation-session combinator owns the capture/plan/apply/retry protocol — retry bound, conflict classification, and terminal conflict error live in one place, and command modules contain no hand-written retry loops or per-site conflict arms.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every public plan-producing entry point returns a typed error, and producer failures reach exit-code mapping through typed variants with no stringify-then-downcast round-trip.
- [hard] REQ-03: Journal-action extraction in the transaction kernel is total; the publication path contains no `unreachable!` panic sites.
- [hard] REQ-04: The initialize and profile-application request variants flow through the shared plan-identity tail, or a recorded decision item states why they are exempt.
- [hard] REQ-05: Property-based tests cover plan-hash determinism under action reordering and managed-document splice round-trip.
- [hard] REQ-06: The cutover guard enforces publisher visibility restrictions instead of source-text substring matching, while the deleted-module assertions are retained.
- [hard] REQ-07: Multi-threaded contention tests cover concurrent mutation-session opening and active-layout reentry rejection.
- [hard] REQ-08: Well-known repository file paths are compile-time constants, and repair-path test coverage derives from the repair planner's own declaration rather than a hand-maintained list.
- [hard] REQ-09: A checked-in benchmark harness records repeated runs with machine and cache-state metadata as artifacts at a stable path, and every published timing claim traces to such an artifact.
- [hard] REQ-10: Session-open budget tests bound bulk update to eligible work, matching the guarantee already tested for automatic transitions.
- [hard] REQ-11: The per-session cost profile is recorded as an artifact, and the lock-hygiene approach chosen from that profile is implemented so zero-byte lock files no longer accumulate without bound.
- [hard] REQ-12: Test-only failure-injection and fixture surfaces are feature-gated out of the default library surface, dead exports are removed, and public items with no external consumer are demoted to crate visibility.
- [hard] REQ-13: The repository-state store's inline test module lives in a sibling file, and tests named after review rounds follow the `test_<function>_<scenario>` convention.
- [hard] REQ-14: A contributor architecture document covers the repository-state/materialization subsystem, and the stale storage-abstraction pointer in the core system design document is swept.
- [hard] REQ-15: The five advisory-debt items recorded at the predecessor epic's completion are cleared from the codebase and documentation.
- [hard] REQ-16: A corrected successor presentation of the repository-materialization story exists in which every falsifiable claim traces to a repository artifact, and the predecessor deck is archived with a tombstone pointing to the successor and the audit.

## Decisions

- D-1: The full audit remediation scope (Part C groups C1–C5) lands in this one epic; the presentation work is a corrected retelling of the predecessor story, not a deck about this epic's own work.
- D-2: The epic ships in milestone v1.0 at high priority and blocks the release: the production-readiness epic depends on it.
- D-3: The predecessor showcase deck is superseded, archived with a tombstone that points to the successor presentation and the audit.
- D-4: The audit document is imported to `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md` and linked to this epic as its citable evidence source.
- D-5: Epic completion evidence includes a genuinely independent holistic review performed by a reviewer distinct from the building agent, enforced as a required gate rather than self-attested narrative.
- D-6: The benchmark harness is a maintained contract — checked in, repeated runs, recorded environment, artifact-backed timings — not a one-off measurement.
- D-7: The lock-hygiene design (consolidation versus lazy creation) is decided from the session-cost profile during planning, before implementation fan-out, and recorded as a plan decision.

## Notes

Finding-level detail, evidence pointers, and the reference index live in `dev/studies/cdc840ad-audit-2026-07-23.md`. Cross-cutting constraints: `@/inv/derived-state-coherence`, `@/inv/atomic-writes`, `@/inv/semantic-test-assertions`, `@/inv/shared-test-contracts`, `@/inv/bounded-rust-build-footprint`, `@/charter/D-14`.
title: Repository-state quality hardening
